name: calls/decode
doc: the decode call's contract, the facts that do not depend on the depth: every (d_v, decay) FSLA accepts, the call's kind (decode: `prefill` 0, one token, a state in and out) and the extents it is sized by (`batch_heads`). A list is alternatives, each its own context; a range is one context. d_v is a range because the seam pads any value width up to the arm that serves it (decode's launch function maps d_v into the arm's, common/plan/decode_launch.h). The depth and the level widths are a depth part's (calls/depth1 .. calls/depth4), composed beside this one.

d_v.declared_by: docs/internals/decode/arms_gen.md#the-contract: the value widths a decode arm serves, 2 up to its widest arm; fsla/_state.py's StateFormat admits an even width from 2

decay.declared_by: docs/internals/decode/arms_gen.md#the-contract: the recurrence either decays (1) or not (0)

prefill.declared_by: docs/internals/common/plan/decode_launch.md: this part is the decode step's call: the prefill fact is 0 (a prefill's parts are the owed descriptors', hardware/descriptors/owed)

tokens.declared_by: a decode step consumes exactly one token (fsla/ops/decode.py `_fold`)

batch_heads.declared_by: docs/api.md#batch-heads: a decode step serves B times H from 1 to 536870911, the largest the step's work queue indexes (csrc/fsla/src/decode/decode.cu: `int BH` and the queue of 4 B H + 2 int32 counters)

stateful.declared_by: a decode step continues a sequence: a state is handed in and out (fsla/_state.py `_require_carrying`)

dense_plane.declared_by: fsla/ops/produce.py decode_descriptor: the decode step takes its backing from the state it is handed, so the pin is not read; either value is a lawful call

memory_budget.declared_by: fsla/ops/produce.py decode_descriptor: a decode step allocates no working set beyond its sequence's scratch, so a declared budget is not read; any value is a lawful call
